neet_che_u17_t06_1.working: The carbonyl carbon forms three sigma bonds and one pi bond. That makes it sp2 hybridised and trigonal planar, with bond angles of about 120°.

neet_che_u17_t06_2.working: Propan-1-ol hydrogen-bonds, so it boils highest. Propanal is polar and has dipole-dipole attractions, so it comes next. Butane is nonpolar and boils lowest.

neet_che_u17_t06_3.working: The C=O bond is one sigma and one pi bond. Carbon is electron-poor, so it is the electrophilic site; oxygen is the nucleophilic, Lewis-basic site. Carbonyl compounds have larger dipole moments than ethers.

neet_che_u17_t06_4.working: Lower aldehydes and ketones are miscible with water because they hydrogen-bond with water. They have no O-H hydrogen, so they cannot hydrogen-bond with each other. A is true and R is false.

neet_che_u17_t06_5.working: A planar carbonyl group can be attacked from either face, so Statement I is false. The resonance description with a dipolar form is correct, so Statement II is true.
